mechanism: Use two actual rectangular-component families to link houses 1,2,4,5, despite their differing remaining blocks. Targets inferring the same complete inventory from two repeated movable rectangle parts and overlooking the small body of house 2 and flatter roof of house 5. Each color marks a specified input component, rather than an option-letter cue.
mathematical_solution: House 1 and house 4 share the complete inventory: a large square body, tall isosceles roof, one 1x2 rectangular block, one slender rectangular block and three congruent small right-isosceles triangles (the third triangle is rotated over the door in house 4). House 2 has a smaller square body and only two small triangles. House 3 has four small triangles and a much smaller rectangular chimney instead of the 1x2 block. House 5 has a flatter triangular roof. These visible shape/count differences exclude every pair/group except houses 1 and 4, which is A. Colors identify two repeated components only; their boundaries and all distinguishing bodies, roofs and triangles remain unchanged.
human_gate: Only eight existing rectangle contours receive 2pt red/blue style. The complete source house bodies, roof slopes, all small triangles, number badges and every option text remain readable. No relation mark or new building block is added.
